messages.subject: Re: Error in summary (fit, rsquare=TRUE)
parts: The correct usage is rsquare=TRUE rather than resquare=TRUE?
Yes.
When I use resquare=TRUE, it does not display the R-squared value.  Am I right?
resquare= is not an argument to the summary() method for class?lavaan nor class?lavaan.mi objects
I am wondering why it doesn't work for fit<-runMI(model, data=im_sem, fun="lavaan", ordered=c("ST"), estimator="WLSMV")

Versions of lavaan and semTools:

semTools_0.5-6.930 lavaan_0.6-17


It works fine using the help-page example of ordinal data:


data(datCat)
lapply(datCat, class) # indicators already stored as ordinal
## impose missing values
set.seed(123)
for (i in 1:8) datCat[sample(1:nrow(datCat), size = .1*nrow(datCat)), i] <- NA

## impute ordinal missing data using mice package
library(mice)
set.seed(456)
miceImps <- mice(datCat)
## save imputations in a list of data.frames
impList <- list()
for (i in 1:miceImps$m) impList[[i]] <- complete(miceImps, action = i)

## fit model, save zero-cell tables and obsolete "WRMR" fit indices
catout <- cfa.mi(' f =~ 1*u1 + 1*u2 + 1*u3 + 1*u4 ', data = impList)
summary(catout, rsquare=TRUE)


Can you provide a reproducible example? (i.e., with just enough syntax and data to reproduce your error)

messages.subject: Re: Error in summary (fit, rsquare=TRUE)
parts:
Error in lav_standardize_all(object, est = est, GLIST = GLIST, partable = partable,  :
  no slot of name "implied" for this object of class "lavaan.mi"

Thanks for privately emailing a reprex, which helped me narrow it down.
This error occurs only when you have exogenous predictors and ordinal outcomes.  You can avoid it by setting conditional.x=FALSE.  Also, lavaan already sets WLSMV when any outcomes are ordered=.

fit <- sem.mi(model, data=im_sem, ordered=c("ST"), conditional.x=FALSE)
